Kos New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kos, Greece

Not demolished. Jews are recorded on Kos from the 2nd century BCE; Romaniot Jews lived there in the 14th century before expulsion in 1502, with a small community persisting from the start of Ottoman rule in 1522. A synagogue was built in 1747; population reached about 40 families by 1850, dwindling to just 4 families by the early 20th century before postwar recovery and a 1934 rebuilt synagogue (replacing one destroyed in an earthquake). Population reached 166 by 1938, falling to 85-100 by 1943; in July 1944, Kos's Jews were shipped alongside Rhodes's community (2,000 total) to Piraeus, held under brutal conditions at an SS camp near Athens before deportation to Auschwitz-Birkenau and other camps. None of the 12 Kos Holocaust survivors returned to the island. This cemetery's founding is unknown, presumed 20th century.
